acceptance_criteria.criterion: badge-dry-run class exists with background: #f3e8ff; color: #7c3aed; border: 1px dashed #c4b5fd
Dark mode variant exists in [data-theme="dark"] section
Style is visually distinct from other badges

summary: Added .badge-dry-run light mode class (background: #f3e8ff; color: #7c3aed; border: 1px dashed #c4b5fd) after .badge-runner-unknown in styles.css
Added [data-theme="dark"] .badge-dry-run override (background: #2e1065; color: #d8b4fe; border: 1px dashed #7e22ce) in the dark mode section alongside runner badge dark overrides
No tests added — CSS rules are structural and visually verified; existing test suite unchanged (14 pre-existing failures in dialogue/api tests unrelated to this WP)

comments.note: styles.css: The dark mode .badge-dry-run uses #2e1065 background (same as .badge-runner dark) and #7e22ce dashed border. This visually differentiates the dry-run badge from .badge-runner-orchestrator (#1e1b4b) while staying in the purple family. A future design pass could pick a slightly unique dark background to make them fully distinct, but the dashed border is the primary differentiator.

summary: Light mode class exactly matches spec: background #f3e8ff, color #7c3aed, border 1px dashed #c4b5fd. Values verified against acceptance criteria.
Dark mode override at [data-theme="dark"] .badge-dry-run uses #2e1065 background, #d8b4fe text, 1px dashed #7e22ce border. Placement is grouped correctly with the other runner badge dark overrides.

Visual distinctiveness: dashed border style makes this badge immediately distinguishable from all solid-border status and runner badges. Purple color family aligns with the runner badge group, and dashed stroke signals 'not a real run'.
No border-radius specified in the class — correct, as all badge classes in the project rely on the shared .badge base class (pill shape via --radius-pill). Consistent with all other badge variants.
All three acceptance criteria are met. No blocking issues found. PASS.

comments.note: Dark mode .badge-dry-run shares the #2e1065 background with .badge-runner (base runner badge). The dashed border is the primary differentiator, which is effective. An optional future design pass could choose a unique background to make the class independently identifiable without relying solely on the border style. Developer already flagged this as a known trade-off.

notes: CSS badge class added. All three frontend WPs (WP-003 project-detail badge, WP-004 run-log event renderers) can now reference .badge badge-dry-run in their HTML output.

WP-002 CSS badge is approved. Both light-mode (.badge-dry-run) and dark-mode ([data-theme="dark"] .badge-dry-run) variants are present and correct. WP-003 and WP-004 can now reference class="badge badge-dry-run" in their HTML templates.
